'''Stanley Herbert Johnson Jr.''' (born May 29, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] before being selected eighth overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. He has also had stints in the [[NBA]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[San Antonio Spurs]].

==High school career==
A native of [[Fullerton, California]], Johnson was one of the top high school recruits of 2014 by [[Rivals.com]], [[Scout.com]] and ESPN. He was a four-time [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] State champion at [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]]. He played in the 2014 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], 2014 Jordan Brand Classic and the 2014 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He was also a 2014 USA Today first team All-USA Boys Basketball Team selection.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Medina|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150515/nba-draft-stanley-johnson-called-training-with-kobe-bryant-the-hardest-workouts-of-my-life|title=NBA Draft: Stanley Johnson called training with Kobe Bryant the "hardest workouts of my life"|work=DailyNews.com|date=May 15, 2015|access-date=May 15, 2015}}</ref> He scored 2,285 career points at Mater Dei, the third-highest mark in school history behind [[Taylor King]] (3,216) and Tom Lewis (2,456).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.materdeiathletics.org/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=452860&type=d&pREC_ID=1046312|title=All Time Leaders|website=materdeiathletics.org|access-date=April 16, 2020|archive-date=April 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413081623/https://www.materdeiathletics.org/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=452860&type=d&pREC_ID=1046312|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in 2014–15, Johnson was voted first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and was named Pac-12 Freshman of the Year.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx |title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors |work=Pac-12.com |date=March 9, 2015 |access-date=March 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312012307/http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors |archive-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> He started 37 of the 38 games he played for the Wildcats, averaging 13.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.5 steals in 28.4 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/stanley-johnson-1.html|title=Stanley Johnson College Stats - College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|work=SportsReference.com|date=June 26, 2015}}</ref>

On April 23, 2015, Johnson declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Feldman|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/04/24/arizonas-stanley-johnson-last-probable-lottery-pick-to-declare-headed-to-nba-draft/|title=Arizona's Stanley Johnson, last probable lottery pick to declare, headed to NBA draft|work=NBCSports.com|date=April 24, 2015|access-date=April 25, 2015}}</ref> Johnson entered the draft as the 11th ranked prospect on ESPN's Top 100 draft board.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ford |first=Chad |title=Chad Ford's Top 100 |url=https://insider.espn.com/nba/draft/results/top100/_/year/2015 |access-date=April 25, 2015 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Detroit Pistons (2015–2019)===
[[File:Stanley Johnson (31693190665).jpg|thumb|Johnson with the Pistons in 2016]]
On June 25, 2015, Johnson was selected with the eighth overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Langlois|title=Stan takes Stanley: Johnson a big part of Pistons puzzle at small forward|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/stan-takes-stanley-johnson-big-part-pistons-puzzle-small-forward|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2015|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Mayo|title=NBA draft 2015: Detroit Pistons select Arizona's Stanley Johnson with No. 8 pick|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2015/06/detroit_pistons_select_arizona.html|website=MLive|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> In his debut for the Pistons on October 27, he recorded seven points, four rebounds and three assists off the bench in a 106–94 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Newberry|title=Pistons surprise Hawks on opening night, winning 106-94|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/DETATL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2015|access-date=October 27, 2015}}</ref> On November 9, he recorded 20 points and seven rebounds in a 109–95 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Wagaman|title=Curry held to season-low 22 in Warriors' win over Pistons|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151109/DETGSW/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2015|access-date=November 10, 2015}}</ref> On February 4, while starting at [[shooting guard]] in place of the injured [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]], Johnson scored a season-high 22 points in a 111–105 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Trister|title=Pistons blow 27-point lead, recover to beat Knicks 111-105|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160204/NYKDET/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2016}}</ref>

On November 25, 2016, Johnson was suspended for one game without pay by the Pistons for violating team rules.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stanley Johnson Suspended for Violating Team Rules: Latest Details and Reaction |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2678209-stanley-johnson-suspended-for-violating-team-rules-latest-details-and-reaction#:~:text=Detroit%20Pistons%20small%20forward%20Stanley%20Johnson%20has%20been,to%20Keith%20Langlois%20of%20the%20Pistons%27%20official%20website. |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On December 10, he was assigned to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] and was recalled the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Assign Stanley Johnson, Henry Ellenson and Michael Gbinije to Grand Rapids Drive|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-assign-stanley-johnson-henry-ellenson-and-michael-gbinije-grand-rapids-drive|work=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2016|access-date=December 11, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Pistons' Stanley Johnson: Recalled from D-League|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-stanley-johnson-recalled-from-d-league/|work=CBSSports.com|date=December 11, 2016|access-date=December 11, 2016}}</ref> On March 8, 2017, he scored a season-high 17 points in a 115–98 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=George's 3rd-quarter flurry sends Pacers past Pistons 115-98|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900351|work=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017}}</ref> On January 30, 2018, Johnson scored a then career-high 26 points in a 125–114 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Love breaks hand in Cavaliers' 125-114 loss to Detroit|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975493|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2018|access-date=January 30, 2018}}</ref>

On November 9, 2018, Johnson scored a season-high 22 points in a 124–109 win over the Atlanta Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Drummond, Johnson pace Pistons to easy win over Hawks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070850|work=ESPN.com|date=November 9, 2018|access-date=November 10, 2018}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2019)===
On February 7, 2019, Johnson was acquired by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in a three-team trade involving the Pistons and [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire Stanley Johnson, Jason Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-acquire-stanley-johnson-jason-smith|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> On June 26, the Pelicans declined to extend a $4.5 million qualifying offer to Johnson, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pelicans Rumors: Stanley Johnson's Qualifying Offer Declined, Will Become UFA |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2842991-pelicans-rumors-stanley-johnsons-qualifying-offer-declined-will-become-ufa |access-date=March 2, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2019–2021)===
On July 11, 2019, Johnson signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors Sign Stanley Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-stanley-johnson|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2019|date=July 11, 2019}}</ref>

On August 12, 2020, Johnson hit his first ever game winning shot with 4.9 seconds remaining in the 4th quarter against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2019–20 NBA season]] in Orlando. On August 14, 2020, Johnson put up a season high 23 points against the Denver Nuggets coming off the bench in a 117–109 victory. The Raptors made it to the post-season and managed to get to the second round of the [[2020 NBA playoffs|2020 NBA Playoffs]], the first time in Johnson's career that he advanced to the second round. They pushed the [[Boston Celtics]] to 7 games before ultimately falling.

On May 13, 2021, Johnson scored a career high 35 points in a 102–114 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LaVine, Markkanen lead Bulls past Raptors, 114-102|date=May 13, 2021|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307862|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 13, 2021}}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers (2021)===
On September 8, 2021, Johnson signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Free Agents|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|accessdate=September 8, 2021}}</ref> but was waived on October 16, after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|number=1449423925004361728|title=Transactions: We have waived forwards Stanley Johnson and Troy Baxter Jr.|user=chicagobulls|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}}</ref> On November 15, he signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]]<ref>{{cite tweet|author=South Bay Lakers|number=1460307155551014914|title=The #SBLakers have acquired six-year NBA veteran Stanley Johnson. Welcome back to that Cali ☀️|user=SouthBayLakers|date=November 15, 2021|access-date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> where he played six games and averaged 15.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.17 steals per game.<ref name="Bulls10D">{{cite web|title=BULLS SIGN STANLEY JOHNSON TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-stanley-johnson-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2021|access-date=December 9, 2021}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2021–2022)===
[[File:Stanley Johnson (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Johnson with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2022]]
On December 9, 2021, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref name="Bulls10D" /> On December 11, Johnson, along with [[Ayo Dosunmu]], was placed in the NBA's health and safety protocols.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Schaefer|title=Bulls' Ayo Dosunmu, Stanley Johnson Enter Health Protocols|url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/sports/nbcsports/bulls-ayo-dosunmu-stanley-johnson-enter-health-protocols/2705559/|website=NBCChicago.com|date=December 11, 2021|access-date=December 16, 2021}}</ref> He never played a single game for the Bulls before his contract expired.

On December 24, 2021, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with his hometown team, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], via the hardship exemption.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Stanley Johnson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-stanley-johnson-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 24, 2021|access-date=December 25, 2021}}</ref> On January 6, 2022, he was signed to a second 10-day contract,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lakers Sign Stanley Johnson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-stanley-johnson-10-day-contract-1/6/22|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=Los Angeles Lakers}}</ref> and on January 17, he was signed to a third 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers on Twitter: "OFFICIAL: The Lakers have re-signed Stanley Johnson to a 10-day contract."|url=https://twitter.com/Lakers/status/1483148868959162369|access-date=January 17, 2022|website=Twitter}}</ref> Johnson signed a two-year contract with the Lakers on January 26.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Charania |first1=Shams |title=Forward Stanley Johnson has agreed to a new two-year deal |url=https://twitter.com/ShamsCharania/status/1486395167817019398 |website=Twitter |access-date=26 January 2022}}</ref>

On August 25, 2022, Johnson was traded, alongside [[Talen Horton-Tucker]], to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Patrick Beverley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-horton-tucker-and-johnson|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Horton-Tucker and Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=August 25, 2022|accessdate=August 27, 2022}}</ref> On October 15, 2022, Johnson was waived.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jazz Waive Stanley Johnson Ahead of Roster Deadline |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/jazz-waive-stanley-johnson |access-date=October 15, 2022 |website=si.com|date=October 15, 2022 }}</ref>

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2022)===
On December 8, 2022, Johnson signed with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES STANLEY JOHNSON|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-stanley-johnson-2|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2022|access-date=December 8, 2022}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2023)===
On December 12, 2022, Johnson signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Spurs sign veteran F Johnson to one-year deal|url=https://www.tsn.ca/san-antonio-spurs-sign-stanley-johnson-1.1892618|website=TSN.ca|date=December 13, 2022|access-date=December 22, 2022}}</ref> On February 12, 2023, he was waived by the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPURS WAIVE STANLEY JOHNSON|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-waive-stanley-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2023|access-date=February 12, 2023}}</ref>

On February 14, 2023, Johnson was reacquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 14, 2023}}</ref>

===Stockton Kings (2023–2024)===
On December 6, 2023, Johnson was acquired by the [[Stockton Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce Trade|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/stanley-johnson-player-rights-acquired-by-stockton/amp/|website=cbs.com|date=December 6, 2023|access-date=December 13, 2023}}</ref>

===Anadolu Efes (2024–2025)===
On July 4, 2024, Johnson signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stanley Johnson Anadolu Efes’te|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/stanley-johnson-anadolu-efes-te|website=AnadoluEfesSK.org|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 4, 2024|language=tr}}</ref> In February 2025, Johnson was granted permission to temporarily leave the team and return to the United States for family reasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stanley Johnson on leave from Efes for family reasons |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1778716/stanley-johnson-on-leave-for-family-reasons-efes-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=4 February 2025 |language=en |date=31 January 2025}}</ref> On February 11, 2025, Johnson officially parted ways with the Turkish powerhouse and returned to the [[NBA G League]]. In 17 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged only 1.9 points and 1.1 rebounds per contest.

===Nagasaki Velca (2025–present)===
On July 29, 2025, Johnson signed with [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/stanley-johnsons-career-continues-in-japan-he-has-signed-with-nagasaki-velca/|title=Stanley Johnson’s career continues in Japan: he has signed with Nagasaki Velca|last=Martorano|first= Kevin |date=July 29, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 30, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Johnson earned gold medals in the 2011 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]], [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] and [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. Johnson served as [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the 2014 team and earned MVP of the 2014 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_game_05.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703224811/http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_game_05.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 3, 2014|title=USA Basketball Men's U18 National Team Claims 2014 FIBA Americas U18 Championship Gold Medal With 113-79 Victory Over Canada|work=USAB.com|publisher=USA Basketball|date=June 24, 2014|access-date=June 25, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnson was born in [[Anaheim, California]] to Karen Taylor and Stanley Johnson Sr. His parents divorced and his father remarried. Johnson was the couple's only child, and he was raised by his mother in [[Fullerton, California|Fullerton]].<ref name=sondheimer_03152014>{{cite news|first=Eric |last=Sondheimer |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-stanley-johnson-mater-dei-20140316-story.html |title=Mater Dei's Stanley Johnson Jr. goes full-throttle on basketball court |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 15, 2014 |access-date=March 15, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516203203/http://articles.latimes.com/print/2014/mar/15/sports/la-sp-stanley-johnson-mater-dei-20140316 |archive-date=May 16, 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref> His mother played college basketball for [[Jackson State Lady Tigers basketball|Jackson State]], where she was inducted into their Sports Hall of Fame in 2009; she also played professionally in Europe.<ref name=sondheimer_03152014/><ref name=u18_profile>{{cite web|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/johnson_stanley.html |title=Stanley Johnson |work=USAB.com |publisher=USA Basketball |access-date=April 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104174600/http://archive.usab.com/bios/johnson_stanley.html |archive-date=January 4, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Johnson is the stepson of Easter Johnson, and has two brothers and two sisters.<ref name=u18_profile/> Johnson is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mercer |first1=Kevin |title=Stanley Johnson puts 'trust in God' as he seeks longterm role with hometown L.A. Lakers |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2022/01/21/stanley-johnson-trust-god-lakers/ |website=Sports Spectrum |date=January 21, 2022 |access-date=22 January 2022}}</ref>
